## Current State

#3687 moved every ledger reader outside wrap-up onto `_shared/ledger-format.md`'s resolution rule: run `wrap-up-pack.js --print ledger --json {run-dir}/wrap-up-pack-ledger.json`, read `value.files`, treat `value.unattributedFiles` as other runs' ledgers, and take a glob fallback only for a reader with no probe result. Deletion already has a verb (`hooks.js delete-ledger`, resolving through `resolveLedgerPath`), so the delete path inherited ownership and fail-closed behaviour for free, while each reader carries a prose copy of the rule and its edge cases. The build and review of #3687 found six such edge cases in prose (probe failing with `records unresolved` while a run-dir `ledger.md` exists, `unattributedFiles` absent on the run-dir path, append versus flip behaviour on a probe failure, a stale Input table), and the conformance test can only scan sentences for the bare glob, with known escapes (`ALLOWED_RE`, other glob spellings). Evidence: review ledger rows 16-22 and the 3c/3f lens findings on `plugin/skills/ledger/SKILL.md` and `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md`. Cost this session: one review fix round plus a full-suite rerun.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Add a read-side verb (for example `hooks.js resolve-ledger --run <dir>`) that resolves through `bin/lib/wrap-up/ledger-write.js`'s `resolveLedgerPath` and prints this run's ledger path(s), the other runs' ledgers, and a closed set of reports (`found`, `none`, `ambiguous`, `unattributable`), exit 0 like `delete-ledger`
- [ ] Repoint `ledger/SKILL.md`, `review/code-mode-steps.md`, and `_shared/ledger-format.md`'s resolution rule at the verb, keeping the rule's one-paragraph statement and dropping the per-reader edge-case prose
- [ ] Extend `tests/ledger-reader-ownership-conformance.test.js` to pin that a this-run lookup names the verb, replacing the sentence-level glob scan where the verb now decides

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The verb returns the run-dir `ledger.md` when it exists, even when the ownership probe's records are unresolved.
2. The verb never returns an inherited `docs/plans/` ledger as this run's, and reports `unattributable` where `resolveLedgerPath` does.
3. No reader in `plugin/skills` restates the probe's `value.files` / `value.unattributedFiles` handling; each cites the rule.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Ledger readers outside wrap-up resolve this run's ledger through one command instead of per-skill instructions.

Origin: ledger resolve gate from #3687 (items 6 and 22)
Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`tests/ledger-reader-ownership-conformance.test.js` (#3687) fails the suite when a this-run ledger lookup in an instruction step reintroduces the bare `docs/plans/*-ledger.md` glob. It scans one sentence at a time, and three escapes were found by the build's final review and the review lenses (3f pair, 3a): `ALLOWED_RE` exempts any sentence that merely contains "fallback", "inherited", "unattributed" or "other run's", so a reintroduced this-run glob in a sentence that also says "fallback" passes; `GLOB_RE` matches only the literal `docs/plans/*…-ledger.md` spelling, so `docs/plans/*ledger*.md`, the dated `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-*-ledger.md` shape, or `find docs/plans -name "*-ledger.md"` pass; and the sentence splitter merges across a lowercase continuation, so a glob sentence can inherit an exempting word from its neighbour. Closing all three needs a different scan shape (a structural check of which steps are this-run lookups, rather than sentence-level word matching), so it was not fixed inside #3687. Evidence: ledger rows 6 and 22 of the #3687 run and the 3f/3a lens findings on `tests/ledger-reader-ownership-conformance.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Replace the sentence-level `ALLOWED_RE` exemption with a check tied to the rule's own structure (the documented fallback sentence and the prose naming inherited ledgers are listed explicitly; any other glob mention in a ledger-reader step fails)
- [ ] Widen the glob matcher to every spelling of a `docs/plans` ledger lookup (`*ledger*.md`, the dated template shape, `find`/`ls` forms)
- [ ] Add go-red fixtures for each escape above, each failing before the change and passing after, with a message matcher on every `assert.throws`

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A this-run lookup sentence that contains the word "fallback" or "inherited" but is not the documented fallback sentence fails the scan.
2. The `docs/plans/*ledger*.md`, dated-template and `find` spellings each fail the scan when they appear in a this-run lookup.
3. The documented fallback sentence in `_shared/ledger-format.md` and the inherited-ledger prose in `ledger/SKILL.md` still pass.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

The ledger-reader conformance test now catches reintroduced ledger globs however they are spelled.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `tests/ledger-reader-ownership-conformance.test.js` — the scan and its go-red fixtures

Origin: overnight dispatch-fleet coordination session, 2026-10-21

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

When a dispatched attempt fails after `/build` has pushed (a plan commit, say) and its PR is closed, the remote branch `worktree-dispatch-record-{N}` stays on origin. The retry creates a fresh worktree branch with the same name from `origin/main`. `build/adopted-branch-collision-check.md` then classifies origin's tip as `foreign` and stops with `adopted-branch-collision` before any work starts. Auto mode can't silence that HARD-GATE, so the retry is spent.

Seen on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21:
- #3630: attempt 1's PR #3689 was closed with the branch tip at `6a9d5ff`. Attempt 2 collided, and the retry ceiling then applied `bot:blocked` and revoked `auto:build`.
- #3315: attempt 1's PR #3851 was closed with the branch at `9342f0653`, holding only the plan commit `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-21-windows-path-producers-3315.md`. Attempt 2 collided.
- #3488 is set up to repeat it. Attempt 1's PR #3885 closed on `failed: build`, and branch `worktree-dispatch-record-3488` sits at `04948b858` with a plan commit its failure comment says is kept "for the retry".

Each time, someone had to delete the branch by hand before the record could build. The failure comment promises the retry will use the committed plan, but the retry can never adopt that branch.

## Deliverables

- Make a retry of a record whose earlier attempt failed after pushing proceed instead of stopping on its own leftover branch. Do one of the following, and state which and why:
  - (a) On the dispatched attempt's failure path (dispatch Settle, or `two-call-gate.md`'s terminal path), delete the record's own remote branch once its PR is closed, and record any plan commit's sha in the failure comment so the retry can read it.
  - (b) In the collision check, recognize origin's branch as this record's own prior attempt (a closed PR whose head is that branch, for the same record number) and adopt or reset it instead of stopping.
- Either honor or remove the "plan committed for the retry" wording in the failure comment, so it never promises something the retry can't do.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A record whose attempt 1 fails after pushing, and whose PR is closed, is retried by the next dispatch without hitting `adopted-branch-collision`.
- A same-name branch whose PR belongs to a different record, or that has no closed dispatch PR (for example a human's branch), still stops as `foreign`.
- The failure comment's plan-for-retry claim matches what the retry actually does.
- A unit test covers the own-prior-attempt vs foreign distinction, and goes red when that distinction is removed.

## Release Note

Fix dispatched records failing on every retry because their first failed attempt left a branch behind on origin.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/build/adopted-branch-collision-check.md` — own-prior-attempt classification or reference to failure-path cleanup
- `plugin/bin/lib/worktree/remote-branch-collision.js` — classify own prior attempt vs foreign
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/settle-and-merge.md` — failure-path remote branch handling
- `plugin/skills/dispatch/two-call-gate.md` — terminal-path remote branch handling

Origin: reflect full from #3656

## Current State

`build/dispatch.md` copies every SDD `Ruling:` line into the open-items ledger and stages it as `staged/sdd-ruling-{N}.md` for ratify or reverse at the Review Console. SDD writes the bare `Ruling:` form where it decided in lieu of a human, including rulings that defer work ("pre-existing, outside the diff, routed to a follow-up record"). Nothing in that path runs `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s fix-now test or requires a `Defer-reason:` on the staged ruling.

At `autonomy: unattended` the console's `console-resolve.js --policy console-auto` resolves an `sdd-ruling-*` item as ratify, so a deferral that failed no criterion is filed as a follow-up record instead of fixed.

Evidence: #3656's `sdd-ruling-2` (parallel-wave member servers recorded under `spec-{N}/`) deferred a one-file fix that met every fix-now criterion and fell under AC2's literal text ("no ephemeral server outlives the run"). It was caught and fixed at wrap-up only because the wrap-up agent ran the gate by hand against the ruling.

## Deliverables

1. `build/dispatch.md`'s `Ruling:` carry-forward: for a ruling whose one-liner defers work, run `_shared/deferral-gate.md`'s fix-now criteria against the record's acceptance criteria (literal text) before staging. A ruling that qualifies for fix-now is fixed in the build and not staged; one that fails carries a valid `Defer-reason:` header line in its `staged/sdd-ruling-{N}.md`.
2. `console-resolve.js`'s `console-auto` policy: an `sdd-ruling-*` item that defers work and carries no valid `Defer-reason:` resolves `pending` (needs a human) instead of ratify; `wrap-up/review-console-appendix.md`'s `sdd-ruling-*` bullet states the rule.

- A deferral-type SDD ruling that meets the fix-now criteria is fixed during build and does not reach the Review Console.
- A deferral-type `sdd-ruling-*` staged file always carries a valid `Defer-reason:` line.
- Under `console-auto`, a deferral-type ruling with no valid `Defer-reason:` is left pending, never auto-ratified.
- A non-deferral ruling (a settled design decision) resolves exactly as today.
- `npm test` passes in full.

## Release Note

Subagent-driven builds now fix a deferred review finding that qualifies for an immediate fix instead of handing it to the console as a follow-up.

- `plugin/skills/build/dispatch.md` — modify
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console-appendix.md` — modify
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — modify

Origin: reflect full from #3783

## Current State

`plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md`'s `## Arm ready PR` action runs `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` Step 3 (auto-merge) on a green, non-draft PR and states that it "never touches Step 1 (Acceptance labeling)" because item 9 only selects PRs that are already green and not draft.

That reasoning covers Step 2 (Mark ready) and Step 2.5, not Step 1: being green says nothing about whether acceptance labeling (`demo:pending` / the Try it walkthrough) landed. #3783 (PR #3869) made `pr-first-merge.md` Step 1 state that labeling has not landed when the run's `verify.json` is missing or its `acceptance-labeling` row is not `pass`/`skip`, "whichever caller reached this merge", and guarded `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3, but left this third caller as it was (SDD final review Important 3, deferred by ruling 4).

A record-linked `auto:merge` PR armed here whose run skipped wrap-up's Phase 4 merges and closes its record with no demo label, the failure #3712 exposed.

## Deliverables

- `## Arm ready PR` checks acceptance labeling before running Step 3 for a record-linked PR: it resolves the run dir from the PR body's `claude-tweaks-run:` marker and reads `verify.json` (every `spec-*/verify.json` for a multi-spec parent), applying the same landed rule and live-state precheck as `dispatch/close-out.md` step 3.
- When labeling has not landed, the action stages the PR for a human (the record-linked flavor already always stages) with a reason naming the missing labeling, instead of arming it. It never runs labeling itself from a tidy sweep.
- The housekeeping-marker flavor (no linked record) is unchanged: it has no record to label.
- Consider moving the landed check into one helper that close-out, pr-first-merge Step 1 and tidy all cite (e.g. a `verify-results.js`-backed CLI printing landed/not-landed per run dir), so the three callers cannot drift.
- The "never touches Step 1" sentence is corrected to state the guard.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A conformance test pins `## Arm ready PR` to name `verify.json`'s `acceptance-labeling` row before its Step 3 call, and fails when that sentence is removed.
2. The "never touches Step 1 … preconditions already hold" claim no longer appears in `actions-github-issues.md`.
3. A record-linked PR whose run dir has no `verify.json` (and no `demo:pending` on its `Fixes` records) is staged, not armed.
4. `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

`/tidy` no longer arms auto-merge on a record-linked PR whose acceptance labeling never landed.

- `plugin/skills/tidy/actions-github-issues.md` — `## Arm ready PR` checks verify.json acceptance labeling before Step 3
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — Step 1 caller list includes tidy's arm action

## Current State

`plugin/bin/log-decision.js` validates `--reversibility` against the bare enum `high|med|low|n/a` (line 51: `--reversibility must be one of high|med|low|n/a`).

About 75 decision-log templates in `plugin/skills/**/*.md` prescribe a parenthetical note after the enum. Two examples:

- `flow/manifesto.md`'s design-critique row: `Reversibility: n/a (a policy read, not a code mutation).`

- `log-decision.js` accepts a `--reversibility` value of an enum member optionally followed by one parenthesized note. Two examples: `low (divergence persists)` and `n/a (a policy read, not a code mutation)`.
- The written entry renders the value verbatim: `Reversibility: low (divergence persists).`
- A value whose leading token is not an enum member still fails with the existing usage error.
- `formatEntry` and the readers that parse `Reversibility:` (the Review Console and decision-log parsers) keep reading the leading enum token, unaffected by the trailing note.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `log-decision.js --reversibility "low (divergence persists)"` exits 0 and writes `Reversibility: low (divergence persists).`
- [ ] `log-decision.js --reversibility "bogus (x)"` and `--reversibility "lowish"` still exit 2 with the existing usage message.

## Current State

During #3056's build (run `2026-10-21T001740-record-3056`), the dispatched agent ran `claude -p "/doctor prompt-audit"` twice (plus one probe) from inside its own pipeline worktree session. Each nested session ended with a SessionEnd hook event carrying the **parent's** session id (`events.jsonl`: three `session-end` lines, `sessionId` equal to the run's owner), and `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/session-end.js` stamped `run-state.json` `status: interrupted`, `lastEvent: session-end` on the parent's still-running run. The nested session's SessionStart banner then listed the live run as interrupted.

`session-end.js` stamps `interrupted` on `ctx.ownedRun` whenever its attribution is not `fallback`. Ownership resolves by session id, so a child process that runs under the parent's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is indistinguishable from the owner ending. The run recovered only because the agent noticed and re-ran the idempotent `hooks.js record-worktree` restamp; an unnoticed stamp would mislead `check-resume-freshness` and the reconciler.

## Deliverables

1. Reproduce: from a session owning an active run, run a short `claude -p` and confirm the parent run's status flips to `interrupted`.
2. Fix at the source: either have the SessionEnd path distinguish a nested/child session from the owner (e.g. the hook input's own session id vs the inherited env, or a parent-pid marker), or document and enforce that nested `claude -p` runs inside a pipeline session must clear `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` or pass `--bare`-style hook isolation — choose one and record why.
3. Add a regression test in the `tests/hooks-*` suites covering a child SessionEnd against a parent-owned active run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A nested `claude -p` session ending inside an owning session leaves the parent run's `status` unchanged.
- A genuine owner SessionEnd still stamps `interrupted` (existing behaviour preserved).
- The new regression test fails before the fix and passes after; `npm test` passes.

## Release Note

Running a nested Claude Code command from inside a pipeline session no longer marks the running pipeline as interrupted.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/context.js` — ownedRun attribution, if the fix lands there

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect hindsight from #3602

## Current State

`plugin/skills/test/verification.md` (Baseline adjudication) tells every pipeline site to pass `--baseline origin/{integration-branch}` to `bin/verify.js`, so a failing suite is adjudicated against the integration branch's current tip, not against the commit this branch actually forked from.

When the integration branch moves past the branch's merge-base and fixes a test that was red at that merge-base, the branch still carries the red test (it has not merged the fix), the tip passes it, and verify.js reports the inherited failure as `ATTRIBUTABLE` — a false attribution that fails the build.

Observed on #3602 (multi-spec run 2026-10-20T124821): `tests/git-path-read-conformance.test.js` was red at merge-base 160e7c4b3 (#3651's pin vs #3302's line) and fixed on main by a25a47b92 (#3752); the first verify run reported it attributable, and only a hand re-run with `--baseline 160e7c4b3` produced the correct verdict (1 also fails at base, 0 attributable), at the cost of a second full suite run (~4.5 minutes).

## Deliverables

Adjudicate against the branch's merge-base with the integration branch (`git merge-base HEAD origin/{integration-branch}`), either by changing `verification.md`'s prescribed `--baseline` value or by having `verify.js` resolve a `--baseline` branch ref to its merge-base with HEAD.

Keep the existing exit-2 behavior for an unresolvable ref, and state in the report which commit was used as the base.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a branch whose merge-base has a failing test that the integration branch tip has since fixed, and a run that fails only that test, verify.js reports it as also failing at base (0 attributable) and the run passes on adjudication.

Given a test that passes at the merge-base and fails on the branch, verify.js still reports it as attributable.

The report's `baselineAdjudicated.base` names the merge-base commit actually used.

## Release Note

Pipeline verification no longer blames a branch for a test that was already failing where the branch started.

## Technical Approach

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — Baseline adjudication: prescribe the merge-base, not the moving tip
- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — resolve a --baseline branch ref to its merge-base with HEAD (or document why not)

Coverage: no committed rename, new-file, deleted-file or binary patch case; untested `rederive` branches (already-satisfied, unsafe or not-in-patches guards, multi-file partial conflict, rename or delete refusal, numstat or summary failure) and untested CLI `rederiveReason` branches; the console's `checkPatchStack` wiring and its throw fail-closed branch have no test; the order-agreement test mirrors `readSnapshot`'s filter and sort instead of calling it; the `cli.test.js` shadow-refusal test asserts a vacuous `existsSync`. Contract pins and docs: `tests/staged-patch-contract.test.js` pins token presence only, not the re-run-once bound or the re-anchor condition, and its go-red control trips only the heading assertion; the `docs/plugin-structure.md` CLI line does not say exit 2 still prints the JSON line. Scan `headerSources` from the first `diff --git` line only and strip a trailing `\r` from a source name

Make `isUnsafe` reject a `..` segment split on `\` as well as `/`

Give `rederive` a specific refusal reason when the target file is created by an earlier staged patch

Report a `git merge-file` exit above 1 as a git error, not as 'conflict in {path}'

Name every conflict that involves the target in the stacked-check STAGED line, not only the first

Verify `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devNull` on a Windows runner and document or replace the git 2.32 requirement

Add committed `stack-check` cases for rename, new-file, deleted-file and binary patches

Add `rederive` branch tests: already-satisfied, unsafe path, target not in patches, multi-file partial conflict, rename or delete refusal, numstat or summary failure; make the same-anchor rederive test assert the reason, not only `/conflict/`

Add CLI tests for the `rederiveReason` branches: rederive refusal, rederive throw, `--rederive-out` with a non-conflicting target, `conflictsWith` equal to the target

`npm test` passes with no new skips

The #3290 ledger rows 1-15 each name the commit or test that closes them

No user-visible change.

Origin: reflect full from #3026

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

`reconcile --checks` runs exactly the named subset, but `archive` silently depends on `mirror`: `archive-merged.js`'s `localHasMerge` needs the integration branch's merge commit to be an ancestor of `refs/heads/{integration}` or `origin/{integration}`, and only `mirror` (or `remote-prune`) runs the fetch that makes `origin/{integration}` current. A caller who names `archive` without `mirror` gets a silent `local-behind-merge` skip for any PR GitHub merged asynchronously.

Nothing in `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` or `docs/reconcile-checks.md` declares this prerequisite. #3026's drain-termination call was specified as `--checks release,archive,reap`, which would have shipped the defect; it was caught only by the final whole-branch review and corrected to `mirror,release,archive,reap`. The only other scripted subset caller, `_shared/pr-first-merge-post-merge.md` Step 4.2, names `mirror` by hand.

## Deliverables

1. `plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/index.js` declares each check's prerequisite checks (`archive` needs `mirror`, and any other dependency the code shows) and expands an explicit `checks` subset with them before dispatch, preserving the existing dispatch order.

2. `docs/reconcile-checks.md` documents the prerequisite table and that an explicit subset is expanded and runs without the hot-path time ceiling.

3. `tests/reconcile.test.js` pins the expansion: a `checks: ['archive']` request runs `mirror` first; an unrelated subset is not widened.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `reconcile({ checks: ['archive'] })` runs `mirror` before `archive`, and `reconcile({ checks: ['reap'] })` runs only `reap`.

- A dispatch-style call `--checks release,archive,reap` archives a run whose PR GitHub merged asynchronously, with no `local-behind-merge` skip caused by a missing fetch.

- `node --test tests/reconcile.test.js` passes.

## Release Note

Fixed reconcile so naming `archive` in an explicit check list also refreshes the integration branch it needs, instead of silently skipping asynchronously merged pull requests.

`docs/plugin-structure.md:67` states that wall-clock timing budgets live in `perf/` (run by `npm run test:perf`) and never in the default `npm test` suite, because they flake under sibling-suite load. Cost this session: one review finding, one staged patch, one Review Console row; no rework.

A conformance test under `tests/` that scans every `tests/**/*.test.js` for a wall-clock assertion shape (`performance.now()`, `Date.now()`, or `process.hrtime` compared against a numeric budget in the same test body) and fails naming the file and line.

An allow-list mechanism for a deliberate exception, with a required one-line reason, so the gate can be bypassed visibly rather than by deleting the test.

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the pass stamp only for a passing run of the full resolved check set: the write gate requires `fullSet && !parsed.noStamp` (verify.js ~line 568). `plugin/skills/test/verification.md:48` requires any deliberately partial `--cmd` set to pass `--no-stamp`, because the runner cannot tell a partial set from the full one. Why not a single background run: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md:46`'s Foreground rule already permits one full-set run with `run_in_background` when the set exceeds the 600 s foreground cap — but only for the orchestrating session. "A dispatched subagent never backgrounds it — its turn cannot wait on a notification" (the `[IL-108]` family; #1904 stalled waiting on a background verify child's notification that never arrived). `/claude-tweaks:dispatch`'s two-call form runs each `/flow` call as a dispatched subagent, so inside those calls the 600 s cap is hard and chunking is the only sanctioned option. 1. A per-suite stamp mode: `verify.js --stamp-suite` (or equivalent) records, for a passing chunk, which declared checks passed against which sha and tree state, written by the runner only.
2. `--stamp-status` composes `verifiedHead: true` when every check declared in `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` (types, lint, and each declared suite) has a passing per-suite record at the current clean HEAD.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Running each declared check in separate `verify.js` invocations with the per-suite mode, all passing at one clean HEAD, makes `--stamp-status` report `verifiedHead: true`.
2. If any declared check has no passing record at the current HEAD, `verifiedHead` stays `false`.

Long test suites can now be verified in chunks under the 10-minute command limit and still earn a full verification stamp.

Store per-suite pass records alongside the existing stamp (same git-dir location, runner-written), keyed by sha and check name. Have `--stamp-status` compute the full-coverage verdict from the declared check list in `verify-scope.json`. Keep the existing full-run stamp unchanged so current callers see no difference.

Surface: infra

**Related:** #3002

## Current State

`plugin/bin/verify.js` writes the verification pass stamp for any passing full run regardless of tree state (the write gate "never consults dirty", verify.js ~line 547), and `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true` only when the stored stamp was recorded against a clean tree at the current HEAD (`stampCoversCleanHead`, verify.js ~line 125). The dirty value comes from `gitInfo()` in `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js`.

When a check regenerates a tracked file — the reported case is a Next.js production build rewriting `next-env.d.ts` — the tree is dirty at stamp time even though every check passed on the exact HEAD commit. `--stamp-status` then reads `verifiedHead: false`, `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 re-triggers `/claude-tweaks:test`, and the re-run dirties the tree again. The only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out, or a manual restore-and-restamp.

A second, smaller gap from the same report: `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` gives no guidance for a `--cmd` that needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path; the reporter needed two failed runs to learn that a committed wrapper script must put the working directory first on the import path.

## Deliverables

1. `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` accepts a `generated` list of path globs. `verify.js`'s dirty computation for the pass stamp ignores changes to paths matching those globs; any other dirty path still disqualifies the stamp exactly as today.
2. The stamp records which declared-generated paths were dirty at stamp time, so the exemption is auditable.
3. `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` documents the `generated` key (when to use it, and that it must name only files the checks regenerate) and adds a short note on `--cmd` wrappers needing environment variables or a working-directory-first import path.
4. `/claude-tweaks:init`'s verify-scope starter (`plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js`) accepts the new key without breaking existing scope files.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full passing run whose only dirty path matches a declared `generated` glob produces a stamp for which `--stamp-status` reports `verifiedHead: true`, and the stamp lists that path.
2. A full passing run with any other dirty path still produces `verifiedHead: false`.
3. A scope file without `generated` behaves exactly as today.
4. `node --test tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` and the verify CLI tests pass, with new cases for 1–3.

## Release Note

Verification can now earn a passing stamp when a check regenerates a declared generated file, instead of forcing a second run.

## Technical Approach

Extend the verify-scope declaration parser to read `generated`, pass the globs into the dirty computation used for the pass stamp (not the general report's `dirty`, which other readers may rely on), and record the exempted paths in the stamp. Option (b) from the original request — exempting any path that was clean before the run and dirtied by it — is rejected: a check that rewrites source (a formatter or `lint --fix`) would then vouch for a tree that differs from HEAD. Explicit declaration keeps that case disqualifying.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/verify.js` — stamp write and `--stamp-status` dirty handling
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/report.js` — `gitInfo()` dirty computation; add a filtered variant for the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/stamp.js` — record exempted generated paths in the stamp
- `plugin/bin/lib/verify/declaration.js` — parse `generated` from `verify-scope.json`
- `plugin/bin/lib/init/verify-scope-starter.js` — starter scope file compatibility
- `plugin/skills/test/verification.md` — document `generated` and the `--cmd` wrapper note
- `tests/bin-lib/verify/stamp.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- #2806 (untangling `verify/args.js`'s parseArgs, PR #2836) is in flight in the same module family; land after it merges or rebase onto it to avoid conflicts.
- #3002 (per-suite stamps for chunked runs) changes the same stamp format; coordinate the stamp schema so both additions compose.
- The stamp's existing semantics (#1921: the runner is the only writer; #1784: no agent-side writes) must not change.

## Original request

bin/verify.js pass stamp: reads dirty when a check regenerates a tracked file

**Component:** `bin/verify.js` pass stamp (`--stamp-status`, `verifiedHead`) and `test/verification.md` "Verification pass stamp", plugin version 6.134.1.

**Kind:** Gap.

**What happened.** A project's full check list includes a production build of a Next.js app. That build rewrites a tracked, generated type-declaration file (`next-env.d.ts`) in place, so the working tree is dirty at the moment `verify.js` writes its pass stamp. Every check passed on the exact HEAD commit, but `--stamp-status` then reports `verifiedHead: false`, and `/claude-tweaks:review` Step 1.5 treats `TEST_PASSED=true` plus a non-verifying stamp as "re-trigger `/claude-tweaks:test`". Re-running the same full set dirties the tree again, so the only way to a verifying stamp is a second run that leaves the build out.

**Why it matters.** The stamp's dirty rule exists to stop a pass on uncommitted source from vouching for a commit. A file the checks themselves regenerate is a different case, and today it forces a redundant run (minutes of wall-clock per review) or a manual restore-and-rerun on every project whose build touches a tracked generated file.

**Suggested behaviour.** One of: (a) let `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` declare `generated` paths the stamp's dirty check ignores; (b) have `verify.js` compare the dirty set before and after the run and treat paths that were clean before the run and dirtied only by the checks as non-disqualifying, recording them in the stamp; or (c) document the workaround in `test/verification.md` (restore the generated file, then re-stamp with a check set that does not regenerate it).

**Second, related observation from the same run.** A project with no `.claude-tweaks/verify-scope.json` and a Python test list that needs environment variables has no documented way to express `--cmd tests=` other than a hand-written wrapper script, and a script-driven test runner resolves the project's packages differently from `python -m pytest` (the script's directory, not the working directory, is first on the import path). A short note in `test/verification.md` — "when `--cmd` needs environment variables or an interpreter-specific import path, commit a wrapper in the project and put the working directory first on the import path" — would have saved two failed verification runs.

The failure is not a CRLF one: the file passes 8/8 on macOS both normally and under a CRLF-read simulation. Production is unaffected, since the shipped script receives a forward-slashed path from `formatPrintedPath` (per the comment at lines 83-85).

Reuse #3699's established fix, `toPosix(path, sep)` from `plugin/bin/lib/shared-primitives.js`, at the item 1 splice site, and pin it with a win32 simulation the same way #3699 did. ## Current State

The post-merge Windows check on commit 4b3e6fa7f (merged PR #3852) reported two newly failing test files, both on the composed-bundle read-limit rail (`RAIL_BYTES` = 52500, `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/budgets.js`):

- `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` — "rail: every compose call site's max composed bytes fit one Read call" fails with `merge @ wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md:218 52503 B`.
- `tests/wrap-up-merge-mode-conformance.test.js` — "the composed merge bundle stays within the read-limit rail" fails with `wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md:218 composes 52503 B > 52500`.

Re-checked against current `main`, this is still live and is a measurement defect, not real growth. `measureComposed` in `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js` (line 153) reads each compose source with a raw `fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8')` and counts `Buffer.byteLength(compose(...))`. On a Windows `core.autocrlf=true` checkout every source line carries a `\r`, so the count includes one extra byte per line. The same module's `measuredTextBytes` (line 56) already normalizes `\r\n` → `\n` before counting, so the two measurements disagree on Windows. Measured on macOS today: the `merge` bundle is **52129 B** LF (all three call sites: `auto-merge-short-circuit.md:218`, `merge-mode.md:25`, `review-console.md:122`). Under a CRLF-read simulation the same bundle measures **52799 B** and the conformance test fails. The rail is meant as a platform-independent content-size proxy.

**Related:** #3702, #3703, #3742, #3751, #3776, #3797, #3802, #3857, #3886, #3890, #3894

## Deliverables

1. `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js` — `measureComposed` normalizes each source's content `\r\n` → `\n` at read time (line 153), the same normalization `measuredTextBytes` applies, so composed-byte counts are EOL-independent.
2. A regression test in `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` that composes from CRLF-converted copies of real sources (e.g. via `crlfCheckoutRead` from `tests/helpers/read-skill.js`, or a temp-dir fixture) and asserts the composed byte count equals the LF count.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `measureComposed` byte counts are identical for LF and CRLF copies of the same sources. The new test pins it and fails when Deliverable 1's normalization is reverted.
2. Under a CRLF-read simulation, `node --test tests/wrap-up-merge-mode-conformance.test.js tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` passes. Before the fix the merge-bundle rail test fails with ~52799 B.
3. Both files are green on Linux/macOS without the simulation, and the reported LF bytes for the `merge` step are unchanged (52129 B at shaping time, give or take any content change on `main` since).
4. The next post-merge Windows check (`.github/workflows/windows-regression.yml`) lists neither test file.

## Release Note

Fix composed-bundle size checks over-counting on Windows checkouts, which pushed a bundle falsely past its read-limit rail.

## Technical Approach

Normalize at the one raw read in `measureComposed`, matching the module's existing `measuredTextBytes` convention, rather than in each test. Every rail consumer reads `composedBytesReport`, so one fix covers both failing tests. `plugin/bin/lib/compose-context/` (the runtime composer) is out of scope: the rail is a measurement proxy, and the runtime's own bytes are not what these tests pin.

- `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js` — `measureComposed` normalizes CRLF at read (line 153)
- `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` — CRLF-vs-LF composed-bytes regression test
- `tests/wrap-up-merge-mode-conformance.test.js` — no change; passes once the measurement is EOL-independent
- `tests/helpers/read-skill.js` — `crlfCheckoutRead` helper reused (read-only)

- The bundle has only ~371 B of real headroom (52129 of 52500). The Windows failure was masking how close the merge bundle is to the rail, but that is a separate concern from this measurement fix.
- Do not raise `RAIL_BYTES` to absorb the CRLF inflation. The inflation scales with line count, so any fixed bump just moves the false failure to the next bundle that grows.

Re-checked against current `main`, this is a test-side defect and still live. `plugin/bin/claude-tweaks-statusline.js` builds the link with `pathToFileURL(dir).href`. On win32 that resolves the POSIX-style fixture path `/Users/x/Code Workspaces/my-proj` against the current drive, so `file:///D:/Users/x/…` is the correct production output there. The test at `tests/statusline.test.js:259-263` hard-codes the POSIX expectation `file:///Users/x/Code%20Workspaces/my-proj/`. Its sibling "the file:// link ends with a trailing slash" (lines 265-268) hard-codes `file:///Users/x/Code/claude-tweaks/\x07` the same way. The file already has the platform-correct idiom: the `linkedName(dir)` helper (lines 25-26) derives the expected link from `pathToFileURL(dir).href`, and the fallback test at line 256 uses it.

**Related:** #3702, #3703, #3742, #3751, #3776, #3797, #3802, #3857, #3871, #3890, #3894

1. `tests/statusline.test.js` — derive the expected URL in both hard-coded tests (lines 259-263 and 265-268) from `pathToFileURL(dir).href` (directly, or via the existing `linkedName` helper), rather than from POSIX literals. Keep each test's own point explicit: the percent-encoded space (`%20`) and the trailing `/` before the OSC 8 terminator.

1. Neither renderProject URL test contains a `file:///Users/...` literal. Both compute the expected link from `pathToFileURL`.

## Technical Approach

Reuse the file's own `linkedName`/`pathToFileURL` idiom for the expected value, so the test asserts the same URL construction production uses on each platform.
